plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem and a showy flower head made up of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk packed with tiny fertile florets. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, a behavior called heliotropism.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated across the United States, Ukraine, Russia, France, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Mature sunflowers stop tracking the sun and permanently face east, which warms the flower in the morning and attracts more pollinators.

plants.name: Hydrangea paniculata
plants.description: A hardy deciduous shrub that produces large cone-shaped clusters of flowers. The blooms start creamy white or lime green and age to pink, rose, or burgundy as late summer progresses into fall.
plants.location: Native to China, Japan, and Sakhalin Island; grown in temperate gardens in North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Unlike bigleaf hydrangeas, panicle hydrangeas bloom on new wood, so they reliably flower even after harsh winters.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower of meadows, roadsides, and prairies that forms dense colonies. It produces arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads that are a crucial late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other insects.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects; the true culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, made of a central cone of tiny flowers surrounded by showy, petal-like bracts. It thrives in the nutrient-poor, acidic soils of the fynbos.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August to November), with peak flowering in spring
plants.location: Native to the Western and Southern Cape of South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its ancient lineage predates the breakup of the Gondwana supercontinent.
